title: Marketplace onboarding docs update plan (AWS + GCP) — DevEx
content:
Objective
- Publish clear, accurate AWS + GCP Marketplace onboarding guidance on docs.redwoodinference.com that matches the new marketplace SKUs and the updated purchase → entitlement → org linking flow.
- Reduce support tickets by making the “what do I do next?” path explicit, including entitlement lag, wrong org, and region mismatch troubleshooting.
- Ensure security/compliance statements are consistent across listing copy, security FAQ, and docs (no over-claims).

Non-goals
- Rewriting the entire Getting Started guide.
- Replatforming docs IA. This plan focuses on minimal, obvious entry points and reducing dead ends.

Audience / use-cases (what we’re optimizing for)
1) Procurement-driven buyer who already knows they must purchase via AWS/GCP Marketplace and needs exact steps + what to provide their admin.
2) Engineer who just purchased (or was told “we bought it”) and needs to activate entitlements fast.
3) Solutions Engineer helping a buyer through “we can’t see the subscription / our org doesn’t have access.”
4) Existing Redwood customer moving spend to marketplace: understanding mapping, entitlements, and plan transitions.

Information architecture (where marketplace guidance lives)
Primary pages (new)
A) /billing-and-procurement/aws-marketplace
- AWS-specific purchase and activation steps.
- AWS entitlement timing expectations and how to confirm purchase.
- Org linking walkthrough in Console.
- AWS-specific troubleshooting (multiple AWS accounts, payer vs linked accounts).

B) /billing-and-procurement/gcp-marketplace
- GCP-specific purchase and activation steps.
- GCP validation / region selection differences.
- Org linking walkthrough.
- GCP-specific troubleshooting (region mismatch, project vs billing account confusion).

C) /billing-and-procurement/marketplace-faq
- Shared FAQ for both marketplaces (billing, upgrades/downgrades, support, refunds where applicable).
- Explicit “AWS vs GCP differences” section with a small comparison table.

Secondary updates (existing pages to link into marketplace pages)
- /pricing (add a “Buying via marketplace” section and link to A/B/C)
- /getting-started (small callout: “Purchased via AWS/GCP Marketplace? Start here.”)
- /security (link to marketplace security FAQ and shared responsibility statement)
- Console in-product links: from onboarding wizard and entitlement status screens → relevant docs anchors (owned by Console team, but DevEx provides final URLs and anchor ids).

Navigation
- Add “Billing & Procurement” left-nav category if it doesn’t exist; otherwise add “Cloud Marketplace” subsection.
- Keep SEO-friendly slugs; avoid embedding “v2” or date in URLs.

Doc requirements (what each marketplace page must include)
Each of /aws-marketplace and /gcp-marketplace must include:
1) Prerequisites
- Redwood account + org required (or how to create one).
- Admin permissions required in AWS/GCP marketplace.
- Who should do what (procurement vs engineer) in 2–3 bullets.

2) High-level flow diagram (one diagram reused with AWS/GCP labels)
- Purchase in marketplace → entitlement event → Redwood entitlement ingestion → Console org linking → active plan/entitlements.
- Annotate “typical timing” and note that timing may vary.

3) Step-by-step activation
- Step 1: Confirm purchase/subscription
- Step 2: Open Redwood Console → Marketplace setup
- Step 3: Link subscription to a Redwood org (or create org)
- Step 4: Confirm entitlement state (Active / Pending) and next actions
- Step 5: Validate with a simple API call (include curl + SDK snippet)

4) “Common gotchas” callout box
- Multiple cloud accounts (payer vs member) / multiple GCP projects.
- Wrong org linked.
- Region mismatch (especially for GCP flow).
- Entitlement lag (what to do after X minutes; when to contact support).

5) Troubleshooting section with decision tree
- Start with “I can’t see my entitlement” → checks → escalation.
- Provide “What to send support” template (Subscription ID / AWS account id / GCP billing account or project id / Redwood org id / timestamp).

6) Links out
- Link to shared FAQ.
- Link to security FAQ (marketplace-specific) with disclaimers.
- Link to support contact path.

Required diagrams / visuals (what we need and who owns them)
1) Purchase → entitlement → org linking sequence diagram (docs)
- Format: simple SVG/PNG (dark + light background safe), plus text-only fallback in the page.
- Owner: Elliot Price (DevEx) with review from Ethan Park (entitlements) + Chloe Martin (Console).

2) Console screenshots (AWS + GCP)
- Screens needed (minimum):
  a) Marketplace setup entry point (where user clicks)
  b) Org linking screen (choose/create org)
  c) Entitlement status screen (Active vs Pending example)
  d) Error state screenshot (region mismatch or invalid subscription)
- Owner: Kira Thompson (screenshots), with redaction review by Marcus Lin (security) and PMM (Soojin Lee) for UI polish.
- Notes:
  - Must not show customer names, emails, tokens, internal IDs that aren’t safe.
  - Use “Acme Demo Org” and seeded test subscriptions.

3) AWS vs GCP comparison table (docs)
- Can be a table only (no screenshot). Keep it brutally clear.
- Owner: DevEx; validate with Partnerships/PM.

New quickstarts (docs + repo)
Goal: a dedicated “marketplace buyer path” that an engineer can complete in <10 minutes after procurement.

Quickstart 1: “Validate your marketplace entitlement (Hosted API)”
- Steps:
  - Link org
  - Create API key
  - Run a single generation request
  - Check usage page
- Deliverable: docs page + optional CLI command snippet if available.
- Repo linkage: redwood-quickstarts PR (tracked in GitHub:redwood-quickstarts/pr-911)

Quickstart 2: “Dedicated / Private next steps after marketplace purchase”
- The marketplace purchase is procurement; Dedicated/Private still requires capacity/network provisioning.
- Provide:
  - What info Redwood needs (region, VPC/VPC peering requirements, SSO, KMS preferences)
  - What the customer should expect (timeline, kickoff)
  - Link to Mutual Action Plan template (internal-facing link for SE/CS; external doc sanitized)
- Owner: Kira Thompson w/ review from Lauren Bishop (Dedicated PM) + Vivek Kulkarni (Private PM).

FAQ content (shared)
Marketplace FAQ must answer (at minimum):
- How does marketplace billing work vs direct contract?
- Can we use committed spend / PO through marketplace?
- Can we change SKUs (upgrade/downgrade)? What happens to existing usage?
- Are add-ons separate line items? (retention/compliance/premium SLA if applicable)
- Refunds/credits: what Redwood can/can’t do (keep language conservative; align with Finance/Legal).
- Support: where to file tickets; what “entitlement pending” means; escalation expectations.

Security/compliance language guardrails (must-follow)
- Only state what we can evidence. Avoid “zero data retention” or “fully isolated” unless the security packet explicitly supports it.
- Use shared responsibility model language: marketplace purchase does not change customer responsibilities for cloud account governance.
- Refer readers to “Marketplace security FAQ” for specifics on encryption, audit logging, and retention controls.
- Marcus Lin is final reviewer for security phrasing and screenshot redaction.

Docs repo implementation notes
- Use a shared include/partial for the “What to send support” template and “Entitlement pending” explanation to keep AWS/GCP pages consistent.
- Add stable anchors for Console deep links (e.g., #link-your-subscription, #entitlement-pending).
- Add redirects if we move older marketplace content (keep old URLs working through launch).
- Add simple page-level analytics tags (UTM-friendly links from listing copy).

Ownership + review process
Primary DRI (docs): Elliot Price
- Responsible for IA, final content quality, and merging.

Section owners
- AWS marketplace page: Elliot Price (draft) + Ethan Park (technical validation)
- GCP marketplace page: Elliot Price (draft) + Ethan Park (technical validation)
- Dedicated/Private quickstart: Kira Thompson
- Screenshots: Kira Thompson (capture) + Marcus Lin (redaction/security) + Soojin Lee (messaging)
- Support templates / troubleshooting decision tree: Dev Patel (support) provides inputs; DevEx writes final docs

Review checklist (before merge)
- Technical correctness validated by Entitlements/Console owners.
- Security claims approved by Marcus Lin.
- Links: no broken links; Console links point to production paths.
- Screenshots: redacted, consistent UI theme, readable.
- Copy aligns with marketplace listing messaging framework (Soojin Lee review).

Milestones / timeline (targeting marketplace listing go-live)
Week 1
- Draft IA and page skeletons (AWS/GCP/FAQ)
- Define required screenshots list + seed data requirements

Week 2
- Fill AWS/GCP step-by-step activation content
- First pass troubleshooting decision tree
- Start screenshots capture in staging

Week 3
- Add quickstart(s) + validate commands
- Integrate Console deep links/anchors
- Security copy pass + redaction review

Week 4
- Final edits, redirects, nav placement
- Publish timed with listing go-live

Open questions / dependencies
- Final SKU names and add-on packaging language (waiting on PM/Packaging final sign-off).
- Exact Console IA for marketplace setup entry point (depends on Console onboarding wizard final UI).
- SLA/retention/compliance add-on terminology: ensure it matches billing UI and marketplace listing fields.
- GCP region mismatch behavior: confirm exact error messaging and recommended remediation steps.

Appendix: “What to send support” template (draft)
Subject: Marketplace entitlement activation issue
- Cloud: AWS | GCP
- Marketplace subscription/offer name:
- Subscription ID (AWS) / Billing account + project (GCP):
- Cloud account id (AWS) / Org + billing account (GCP):
- Redwood org name + org id:
- Timestamp of purchase + timezone:
- Screenshot of entitlement status page (redacted):
- Any error message text:

Appendix: baseline SLA for docs updates post-launch
- DevEx will maintain these pages for 60 days post-launch (bugfixes + clarity improvements).
- After stabilization: move to normal docs ownership rotation; Support and Partnerships continue to feed issues via Slack #docs + monthly marketplace retro.
